title: Kaju Katli for Diwali: Cashew, Sugar and Ghee, Cut Into Diamonds
excerpt: The classic cashew fudge needs three ingredients and one judgement call — the one-string syrup. Two tested recipes, the powder method, and how long it keeps.
body:
• Kaju katli is a cashew fudge of three ingredients — cashews, sugar and a little ghee — rolled thin and cut into diamonds; katli means thin slice.
  • The method that keeps it smooth: powder room-temperature cashews without over-grinding, and add them only when the sugar syrup reaches one-string consistency.
  • Raks Kitchen's proportions are 1 cup cashews to ½ cup sugar and ¼ cup water, making about 14 pieces in 10 minutes of prep and 20 minutes of cooking.
  • It keeps 5 to 7 days at room temperature and up to two weeks refrigerated — but only 3 days if you added milk while kneading.

Kaju katli is the sweet that fills Diwali gift boxes: a smooth cashew fudge, rolled thin, cut into diamonds and, in sweet shops, topped with silver leaf. It is also genuinely makeable at home. As Raks Kitchen's recipe puts it, the sweet uses only three ingredients — cashew nuts, sugar and a little ghee — and gives a sweet-shop texture once three things are understood: never grind cold cashews from the fridge, knead the warm dough for the smooth finish, and get the syrup consistency right. The word katli means thin slice, which is what the diamond pieces are.

The method

Start with 1 cup of cashews at room temperature and powder them in a dry mixer in one stretch, stopping as soon as the powder appears in the lid — grind longer and the nuts release oil and turn lumpy. Make the syrup from ½ cup sugar and ¼ cup water over gentle heat, testing as it nears the stage: a few drops in a bowl of water should lay a fine thread that does not dissolve immediately, or stretch into a single string between finger and thumb. Lower the flame completely, add the cashew powder and stir continuously for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture thickens and leaves the sides of the pan. Test a pinch between greased fingers — it should roll into a soft, non-sticky ball. Move the warm mixture to a greased tray or parchment and knead: it looks grainy at first and turns smooth as you work it. If it is dry, sprinkle a little milk and keep kneading, as Raks Kitchen does; a slick of ghee on gloves helps too. Roll thin and cut diagonally into diamonds, scoring the lines lightly with the knife tip first. Allow the pieces to cool completely before lifting them.

Variations and fixes

Healthy Indian Recipes' version uses slightly more sugar — ¾ cup sugar and ⅓ cup water to the same 1 cup of cashews — and finishes the dough with 1 teaspoon of ghee and ¼ teaspoon of cardamom powder, rolling to about a quarter-inch thickness and decorating with optional silver leaf. Raks Kitchen notes ⅛ teaspoon of cardamom powder or rose water can be added for flavour. If the finished mixture is dry, sprinkle a teaspoon of milk; if it is sticky or wet, a tablespoon of unsweetened milk powder firms it up. The classic version uses no milk or condensed milk in the dough itself, which is what gives it its shelf life.

Storage

Kaju katli stays good for 5 to 7 days at room temperature in an airtight container once completely cooled, and up to two weeks in the refrigerator. The exception matters during Diwali week: if you sprinkled milk while kneading, eat those pieces within 3 days and keep them refrigerated. That is the whole case for making it at home — a small batch, made in about half an hour, that tastes of cashew rather than of the box it came in.

Boil the sugar with the water, stirring, until the syrup reaches one-string consistency: a drop stretched between finger and thumb forms a string that does not break.
Lower the flame completely and add the cashew powder, stirring continuously for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
Test a tiny portion between greased fingers: you should be able to roll a soft, non-sticky ball.
